business_question: Do US semiconductor export controls create hidden revenue concentration risk for NVIDIA in its largest growth market?
description: NVIDIA derives significant revenue from data center customers in China. US Bureau of Industry and Security export control regulations (BIS Entity List, October 2022 and subsequent updates) restrict the sale of advanced AI accelerators including A100 and H100 to Chinese customers without a license. NVIDIA's attempt to create compliant variants (A800, H800) was subsequently also restricted. An investor holding NVIDIA may not recognise that regulatory action by a single government agency can materially impair access to a market representing a substantial portion of data center revenue.
current_state_notes: NVIDIA currently qualifies for a Blind Spot through the existing Supply Chain path (NVIDIA → TSMC → Taiwan → Taiwan Geopolitical Risk), which uses the same reasoning pattern as apple_taiwan. The export controls path requires three Atlas nodes that do not yet exist: china as a SELLS_TO target, us-bis-export-controls as a REGULATION node, and semiconductor-export-ban as an ECONOMIC_EVENT. This case becomes State A once those nodes and relationships are added.
future_expansion: Add HBM memory supplier concentration (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron) as a Supplier Concentration case
Add ASML dependency through TSMC as a second-order Supplier Concentration case
Add EU AI Act as a separate Regulatory Risk case once enforcement begins
